Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for prod (eastus2)

Naomi,

We just observed a sudden latency spike and a rise in 5xx errors for our production traffic routed to eastus2 (region: eastus2a, AZ?). Impact began ~08:55 PDT and is still ongoing. Throughput dropped ~30% and p50 token latency jumped from ~120ms to ~650ms for several endpoints.

Sample error window: 08:56–09:10 PDT. I attached a Grafana screenshot and a small log extract showing connection resets to the GPU-workers.

This is affecting our scheduled batch ingestion and user-facing flows. Can you escalate? We need an ETA for resolution or a routing workaround.

Att: grafana-spike-0901.png (image/png), deployment-logs-eastus2-0901.txt (text/plain)

-Carlos

Subject: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for prod (eastus2) — immediate triage

Forwarding Carlos' note — Novus is seeing token-latency and throughput degradation in eastus2. Please treat as P0. Quick asks:

- Ben/Jonas: triage and confirm root cause (networking vs serving). If eastus2 AZ is flapping, prepare controlled redistribution to westus3. I attached a short traffic-redistribution playbook.
- Sean/Marissa: hold customer comms cadence (acknowledge, ETA, and then mitigation update at +30m).
- I will loop in SRE leadership and prepare exec brief if we need credits/SL escalation.

Planned immediate steps (proposed):
1) Verify eastus2 instance health and recent K/V cache invalidations.
2) Snapshot current routing policy and prepare rollback.
3) Start 10% canary routing to westus3 for low-latency customers, monitor errors for 10m, then escalate to 50% if stable.

Meeting in 20m (09:45 PDT) unless we resolve in-thread.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-01T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for prod (eastus2) — immediate triage

Naomi / team,

Prelim diagnosis: eastus2's serving subnet is exhibiting transient network flaps between the hsm-router and some GPU nodes. We see a spike in TCP resets and increased retransmits which explains the elevated token latency and 5xxs. No model regressions.

Quick mitigation plan I can execute now:
- Step A (0–6m): mark affected AZ pool as degraded in the router and remove from weighted pool hairpinning (no reboot required).
- Step B (6–20m): begin controlled redistribution: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% as long as error rate <= 0.5% and p50 latency <= 250ms.
- Step C (after stable): re-balance prefixes and flush KV cache for the moved sessions.

Commands (internal):
1) rtrctl set-pool-state eastus2a degraded --reason "net-flap"
2) rtrctl update-weights novus-prod westus3=0.1 eastus2a=0.9

Estimated time to 60% redirection if green: ~18 minutes. I'll start Step A now and post status updates.

Attaching collected logs fragment for your reference.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Carlos / Anya — quick update from Redwood: we acknowledge the issue and have an active mitigation in progress.

What we are doing now:
- SRE has flagged the eastus2 AZ as degraded and initiated a controlled redistribution of traffic away from eastus2 to westus3.
- The redistribution is staged: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> full. Each stage has a 10-minute validation window.

Expected customer impact: brief reconnections for some long-running sessions; most requests will see progressively lower latency as traffic moves. We'll update you at +15m and again when we reach 60%.

Meeting: I've booked a 30-minute bridge at 10:00 PDT in case you want real-time updates: https://meet.redwood.com/novus-incident-0901

Thanks for flagging — will follow-up with timeline.

— Sean

Subject: Novus — incident summary, mitigation timeline, and next steps

Carlos / Anya,

Thank you for your patience during yesterday's incident. Below is a short executive summary and proposed remediation path.

Timeline summary (PDT):
- 08:55: Novel latency and 5xx spike observed in eastus2 (customer report).
- 09:22: Redwood SRE engaged, eastus2 AZ marked degraded; redistribution plan drafted.
- 09:31–10:05: Controlled redistribution executed; reached 60% by 10:05 with error rate <=0.4%.
- 10:30: Stabilization confirmed; continuing monitoring.

Impact: temporary increased latency and reduced throughput for ~20–40% of traffic for ~35 minutes; no data loss observed.

Root cause (prelim): transient networking flaps at the AZ level causing connection resets to serving nodes. Full RCA pending deeper infra vendor logs.

Short-term remediation we recommend:
1) Keep the diversified routing weights for Novus while we validate for 24 hours.
2) Implement an automatic fallback rule: if p50 token latency > 300ms AND 5xx_rate > 0.5% for >5m, shift 30% traffic to fallback region.
3) Offer a one-time 10% credit for September's usage as a gesture; let us know if you'd prefer an alternative (service credit vs technical support hours).

Attachments & artifacts: grafana-spike-0901.png, deployment-logs-eastus2-0901.txt, traffic-redistribution-plan-0901.pdf
Related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721, https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/novus-incident-0901

We are scheduling a postmortem and will share the draft RCA in 72 hours. Please let us know whether 16:00 PDT today is a good time for an executive sync with our Head of Reliability (Jonas).

Appreciate the partnership — Naomi
